description.narrative:
The Horn of Africa Regional Environment Centre and Network ((HoAREC&N) Regionalt Miljöcentrum och Nätverk på Afrikas Horn)) har ansökt om 78,600,000 SEK för att genomföra ett femårigt regionalt projekt " Miljömässig hållbarhet och resiliens på Afrikas Horn". Insatsperioden är från oktober 2019 till december 2023. Insatsens fokus är i huvudsak att stödja ett integrerat multidimensionellt tillvägagångssätt inom landskapsplanering och utveckling i fyra utvalda landskapsområden; a) Kafta - Shiraro och Gash-Setit (KS-GS) (mellan Etiopien och Eritrea) ett socioekologiskt landskap b) Sydvästliga 'Rift Valley' - ett ekologiskt gränslandskap mellan Etiopien, Kenya och Sudan (SWRV-SEL); c) Lake Abbe och Lake Assal-Dafo (LAA) ett gränslandskap mellan Etiopien och Djibouti och d) Geed-Deeble landskap (Geed Deeble-Botaniska trädgård) (Somalia). De geografiska landskaps områdena a)-d) har valts då de anses ha en hög ekonomisk potential för social transformation, god regional miljömässig styrning, stora utvecklingsmöjligheter för ett regionalt samarbete och att främja regionens fredsbyggande. Insatsen består av fem tematiska områden: Förbättrade diversifierade levnadsvillkor, livsmedelstrygghet och motståndskraftiga samhällen 2) främjande av restaurering i känsliga habitat, naturresursförvaltning och ökad landskaps motståndskraft 3) främja publikt-privat-partnerskap (PPP), ökat kunskapsutbyte, policy dialog och stärkande av evidensbaserat politiskt beslutsfattande 4) främja nyttjandet av förnybar energi och energieffektiv teknologi och 5) bygga regional och lokal kapacitet vilken identifierats som framgångsrik för att tillämpa denna i de fyra utvalda geografiska områdena.
Under de första sex månaderna genomförs en förstudie för att konsolidera projektplanen. För att bestämma insatsens baslinje samlas data och nödvändig information in. Sakägarna sammankallas och deras formella deltagande säkras. Projektplanen utvärderas och bedöms i sin helhet och insatsen lanseras formellt och operationaliseringsfasen tar vid. Följaktligen så kommer en godkänd projektplan och budget att arbetas fram av HoAREC& N som fokuserar på de förbättringar som föreslagits under insatsens förberedande fas. Vid avslut av förberedelse fasen så kommer HoAREC & N att lämna in den reviderade projektplanen inklusive budget för den fortsatta insats perioden tillsammans med en detaljerad projektplan och budget för vart och ett av de fyra valda geografiska gränsområdena. Insatsens totala budget är 78.6 MSEK för perioden oktober 2019 -december 2023 och Sida finansierar insatsen i dess helhet (78.6 MSEK)

The Horn of Africa Regional Environment Centre and Network (HoA-REC&N) has applied to Sida for funding of 78,600,000 SEK to carry out the five years project named "Environmental Sustainability and Resilience in the Horn of Africa" at a regional level during the period October 2019 – December 2023.
The intervention mainly focuses on promoting an integrated multi-dimensional approach to planning and development in four selected intervention landscapes Kafta - Shiraro and Gash-Setit (KS-GS) Transboundary Socioecological Landscape (between Ethiopia-Eretria), Southwest Rift Valley Socioecological Transboundary Landscape (SWRV-SEL) (between Ethiopia, Kenya and Sudan), Lake Abbe and Lake Assal-Dafo (LAA) Transboundary Landscape (between Ethiopia and Djibouti), and Geed-Deeble Landscape (GD-Botanical Garden) (Somalia). The intervention landscapes are selected as they are known for their high economic potential for social transformation and improved regional environmental governance, high opportunity to enhance regional cooperation and promoting peace building in the region. Five thematic components namely: 1) Enhancing livelihood diversification, food security and community resilience, 2) Promoting habitat restoration, natural resources management and landscape resilience, 3) Promoting public-private partnership, knowledge exchange, policy dialogue and evidence-based policy decision making, 4) Promoting utilization of renewable energy and energy-efficient technology and 5) Building regional and local capacity are identified to be implemented across the four intervention areas.
The intervention has introduced a six-month inception phase which will serve as a stepping stone to lay the foundation for the project plan consolidation, baseline data collection and information generation, stakeholder participation and formal engagement, project appraisal and endorsement of project plan and the formal launching of project implementation phase. Accordingly, a separate workplan and budget is prepared by the partner and assessed to be eligible with a specific focus to the issues identified to be addressed during the inception phase. At the end of the inception period the partner agreed to submit a revised work plan and budget for the remaining four and half years as well as detailed budget for each intervention landscape.
The intervention total budget is 78.6 MSEK for the period October 2019 – December 2023, all of which will be contributed by Sida.

The overall objective of the proposed intervention is enhancing environmental sustainability and resilience in the region through research, policy and development as a pathway to promoting sustainable natural resources management, conservation of biodiversity and regional integration, peace and stability in the Horn countries. The intervention principally focuses on promoting an integrated multi-dimensional approach to planning and development in four intervention landscapes (Kafta - Shiraro and Gash-Setit (KS-GS) (Ethiopia-Eritrea) Transboundary Socioecological Landscape, Southwest Rift Valley Socioecological Transboundary Landscape (SWRV-SEL) (between Ethiopia, Kenya and Sudan), Lake Abbe and Lake Assal-Dafo (LAA) Transboundary Landscape (Ethiopia-Djibouti), and Geed-Deeble landscape (GD-Botanical Garden) – Somalia).

In general, during the reporting period the contribution has made significant progress registering countable impacts to increasing social capital and community resilience across the intervention sites. Activities implemented both by the Implementing Partners (IPs) and the coordination activities of HoAREC/N has created the necessary outcome in the transboundary landscapes.
Summary of the achievement
Regeneration of the endangered Yeheb Nut (Cordeauxia edulis) - During the reporting period, Yeheb nut seedlings continued to be propagated. A total of 2,100 young saplings were planted in Walal and Degahbur villages. Meanwhile, efforts to extend the restoration activities to new areas have been successful. Mapping of the endangered Yeheb nut species across the cross-border areas of the Somali Region, Somaliland, and Puntland have been conducted. Technical support and provision of seedlings has been provided to Barwaaqo Voluntary Organization BVO in Somaliland and Rajo Cooperative in Walwal as part of the Horn of Africa (HoA) networking and conservation effort.
Resource assessment has been conducted in Lasdhankerre to evaluate the composition of species and their potential for non-timber forest products (NTFPs). The analysis reveals that much of the area was dominated by Boswellia rivae, exhibiting the highest relative density (RD) of 62.5%, followed by Commiphora myrrha and Giduutti. Acacia Senegal exhibited a lower relative density (RD) of 3.1%. Following the extensive technical evaluation by SoRPARI about the feasibility of frankincense, gum, and resin production in Lasdhankerre Woreda, the project-initiated measures to enhance local livelihoods and promote sustainable resource management.
The project created a prototype cooperative, which received official registration with a regional license. A three-hectare Abrahamic Garden is being established at the Gullele Botanic Garden to symbolize mutual respect among all religious faiths, aiming to enhance connections between religions and the conservation of biological diversity. The Gullele Botanic Garden aims to offer visitors a unique experience by cultivating plant species that has symbolic significance in Christian, Qur'anic, and Judaic sacred writings and religions. The garden has a distinctive role in safeguarding regional biodiversity, facilitating environmental education, and promoting cultural reconciliation.
The establishment of community enterprises in different landscapes has yielded numerous substantial benefits for the communities concerned. The enterprises have created income-generating opportunities for community people, so improving their financial stability and general economic well-being. Model farms have helped to boost local horticulture production, increase access to fresh produce, and improve community food security by diversifying the food supply.
Promising development has been registered towards the establishment of the Lake Abbe Transboundary Protected Area in the landscape surrounding Lake Abbe, which spans the borders of Djibouti and Ethiopia. This is a foundation for environmental conservation and sustainable development improving the livelihood of the communities in the region.
HoA-REC&N has successfully expanded its regional program portfolio by leading the development of a new project titled Managing the impacts of environmental change and conflict on mobility in Eastern Africa (MECMEA). Partners involved include the Association Djibouti Nature, South Sudan Nature Conservation Organisation, Mixed Migration Centre at Danish Refugee Council Kenya, and PanAfricare. Funded by the European Union and the International Centre for Migration Policy Development. This initiative aligns with the broader efforts to enhance cooperation and synergy with the Sida-funded HoA-ESR project. This is unintended results achieved during the reporting period.
The Demand Driven Action Research (DDAR) component of the contribution has been successful helping students and academic staffs develop long-term research capacity and serve as an instrument for collaboration and knowledge exchange among researchers and academic institutions in the Horn of Africa.
During the reporting year, the Demand Driven Action Research (DDAR) grants enabled students and academic staffs to start and complete independent research projects. The DDAR's multidisciplinary approaches have offered an excellent platform for marketing scholarship and internship possibilities for students, as well as a better awareness of the region's environmental policy needs and research prospects. The grant's capacity-building activities were critical in guaranteeing the long-term viability of the research initiatives, as some of those who benefited were university staff who will continue to provide services to the institutions. The research topics and objectives are based on felt need of the communities where the contribution has been implemented. The DDAR continues to provide the needed platform for academic interactions in the region.
The ESR project has created possibilities for networking across Horn countries and beyond by exposing community members to best practices for adoption. Exposure visits allow communities in the different landscapes to observe and learn from effective environmental practices, potentially motivating the adoption of sustainable measures in their businesses. This initiative takes a proactive approach to fostering learning, knowledge exchange, and the adoption of best practices, all of which contribute to a larger effort to combat environmental degradation.
The Public Private Partnership component was very successful in 2024. Two crucial resource sharing agreements has been signed between the villages along the Kenya-Ethiopia border. The Djibouti Association Nature (DAN) has collaborated with Red Sea Power Company, the owner of the Ghoubet wind farm, to assist the local communities living around Lake Assal and Day Forest to offer permanent drinking water as part of its corporate social responsibility and to collaborate with the company to monitor the vulture and bat migratory patterns. In November 2024, DAN and Red Sea Power have signed a five-year service agreement for biodiversity monitoring at the Ghoubet wind farm.
Gender issues have been considered in the provision of early maturing improved crop seeds, the distribution of solar home systems, and the training and support for various livelihood options. The groups underwent a participatory selection process.
The project has enhanced women's empowerment through the establishment of community-led enterprises that develop their skills in sustainable practices, resource management, and leadership roles. This initiative continued to enhance the management capabilities of women. The situation in the Omo and Mago parks' protected areas is a good case to develop further. This is part of the efforts to prevent illegal activities in the park and alleviate pressure on the wildlife resources.
